analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Subaru Park on Saturday 28 November (4:30 pm ET); if New England win Game 1, Philadelphia must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. New England won 2-1 at Subaru Park on 24 October, ending Philadelphia's 15-match unbeaten run, so the site's strong home lean for Philadelphia rests on their wider form more than on this matchup. The view will be refreshed after Game 1.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Both league meetings ended 2-1 and Philadelphia scored four against Toronto in their last home game, which fits a total around three; I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.6 corners, heavily for Philadelphia. Philadelphia at home should have more of the ball, but New England won there in October; I found nothing that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean slightly higher for Game 2: the teams will have met twice in a week, one of them may be facing elimination, and Philadelphia's Jovan Lukic and Ben Bender were both booked against Toronto.

shots.text: The site expects 29.6 shots, with 21.1 for Philadelphia. That is a lot against a New England side that beat them at Subaru Park a month earlier; Philadelphia did take 19 against Toronto, but I lean lower on the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 on target. Matt Turner made the second-most saves in MLS this season, so New England do let shots reach goal, and the Sullivans and Bruno Damiani were sharp against Toronto; I stay with the number.
